title: Racing Santander Aims to Maintain Points Streak Against Alavés
seoTitle: Racing Santander vs Alavés: Points Streak at Stake
subtitle: With 10 points from 12 available, Alavés arrives confident but faces significant absences
excerpt: Racing Santander hosts Alavés in a crucial classification zone match, while the visitors deal with serious injuries to key players Mikel Rodríguez and Facundo Garcés.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The clash between Racing Santander and Alavés, scheduled for this Saturday at 2 PM at the El Sardinero Stadium, has gained prominence following Alavés' performance, which saw them collect 10 out of a possible 12 points in recent rounds. The match becomes crucial for maintaining their position in the qualification zone.

Alavés Arrives with a Strong Points Tally

With 10 points secured from 12 available, Alavés boasts a season start that places them in a comfortable position in the standings. Coach Quique Sánchez Flores emphasized the importance of not letting praise weaken the team, reinforcing the need for focus and humility.

Injuries Affecting Alavés

Two key Alavés players are unavailable due to serious injuries. Mikel Rodríguez suffered a rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament in his right leg, ending his season. Facundo Garcés, who was already serving a suspension for document forgery, also ruptured the same ligament during training, confirming his absence until the end of the season. Toni Martínez has recovered, but he is expected to start the match on the bench.

Racing Santander Seeks to Score Points

Racing approaches the match with four points, the result of one draw, one win, and two losses. The team has shown fragility in its defensive sector, while Alavés stands out for its defensive effectiveness. Coach José Alberto López may opt for changes in the defense, with Pablo Ramón and Belocian as possible starters.

Head-to-Head History

The two clubs previously faced each other in the 2022/23 season, when Alavés won 3-0 at home and drew 1-1 in Santander. In the first division, their last match took place in 2005, with Alavés winning 2-1 at the El Sardinero Stadium.

Match Expectations

Under pressure to maintain their points streak, Alavés intends not to differentiate the importance of playing at home or away, as stated by Sánchez Flores. Racing, in turn, sees the match as an opportunity to improve their position and reduce defensive vulnerability. The outcome will be decisive for the dynamics of the qualification zone at this stage of the competition.
